contentHtml:
Treat each important UX choice as a hypothesis about real use. Verify behavior and observe task completion before concluding that a screen is intuitive.

Three Types Of Evidence

Method What it can establish Limitation
Heuristic walkthrough Likely issues in language, hierarchy, feedback and control Reviewer judgment is not observed user behavior
Functional and accessibility checks Whether specified interactions work in tested conditions Passing selected checks does not prove usability or complete conformance
Usability session How representative people understand and perform a task Findings depend on participants, scenarios and context

Use all three proportionally. For a minor copy edit, a focused review may be enough. A new registration flow needs end-to-end checks and direct evidence about understanding where feasible.

A Lightweight Usability Session

  1. Identify the main uncertainty, such as whether users understand when a record is saved.
  2. Recruit actual or likely users, including relevant roles and access needs.
  3. Give a realistic goal and starting context, using synthetic data.
  4. Let the participant attempt the task without click-by-click instructions.
  5. Observe hesitation, mistakes, recovery, completion and interpretation.
  6. Ask neutral follow-up questions about what they expected and understood.
  7. Fix the most consequential problems and repeat the relevant task.

Example task: A new customer has contacted you. Record their details so a colleague can find them, then correct their phone number.

Avoid: Click Add, enter the fields, press Save and then click Edit. The second script tests following instructions and hides navigation problems.

This method follows GOV.UK moderated usability testing. Synthetic data is this playbook's local default for lightweight sessions; GOV.UK also discusses using participants' real data when appropriate. Any such use needs deliberate handling of access, consent and retention.

Small iterative sessions are useful for qualitative learning. There is no universal five-person guarantee, required percentage of defects discovered or sample size that proves accessibility. Cover materially different user groups and tasks; use a suitable study design for quantitative claims.

When Users Are Unavailable

Review the journey with a colleague unfamiliar with the implementation, use known support evidence and exercise realistic scenarios. Record this as a proxy review. Keep assumptions and the later user-validation opportunity visible; do not relabel a colleague walkthrough as representative research.

Minimum Screen Verification

Check the relevant journey with:

  • keyboard-only navigation, activation, errors and focus recovery;
  • a narrow viewport, zoom, longer translated text and realistic content;
  • representative screen-reader output for labels, states and messages;
  • empty data, many records, missing optional data and permission boundaries;
  • invalid input, duplicate requests, slow responses and server failure;
  • successful persistence, reload, interrupted submission and safe retry;
  • unsaved changes, back navigation and concurrent edits where applicable.

Use existing Testing Standards for repeatable cases. Automate stable, important behavior such as field-error mapping and duplicate effects. Keep human evaluation for whether the labels and flow make sense.

What To Measure

Select measures tied to the goal:

Signal Interpretation
Successful completion The intended result exists and is understood
Assistance or critical errors The flow prevents independent progress or causes wrong outcomes
Time and repeated effort Work that may be reduced, interpreted with task complexity
Abandonment by stage A possible obstacle to investigate, not proof of its cause
Corrections and support requests Understanding or recovery may need improvement

Record denominators and contexts. Report 3 of 4 observed participants for a small session, not an unsupported population success percentage. Do not optimize completion by hiding consequences or making refusal difficult.

Protect Research And Telemetry Data

Collect only evidence needed for the decision. Agree to recordings with participants, set access and retention, and use synthetic data by default. Avoid capturing passwords, field contents or unnecessary personal identifiers in analytics. Session replay requires deliberate privacy review and effective masking, not an automatic default.

Follow Security: Repository and Data Hygiene.

Prioritize Findings

Fix blocked access, data loss, unintended consequential actions and false completion before cosmetic inconsistencies. Then prioritize by task impact, frequency, number of affected people and recovery difficulty. A rare barrier can still be critical for the people affected by it.

Record the issue, observation, context, severity rationale, owner, correction and retest evidence. Keep heuristic concerns distinct from observed failures.

Delivery Evidence

Journey and revision:
Checks performed and environments:
Observed user sessions or proxy review:
Successful and failed scenarios:
Known assumptions and limitations:
Issues resolved and retest evidence:
Remaining issues, owners and review triggers:
